situation: An employer reviewing engineering pay against the market ahead of its annual pay review.
complication: Engineers are paid below market and leave faster than the rest of the company.
key_question: How should the pay review close the engineering pay gap within budget?

titles.situation: Engineering pay sits below the market median.
titles.options: Three ways to close the engineering pay gap.
titles.recommendation: Fund a targeted market adjustment and let the head of people decide each case.
titles.roadmap: Model the adjustment, decide cases, then track leavers.
titles.kpis: Two measures show the gap and turnover are closing.
titles.risks: The main risk is spending the budget where it does not retain anyone.

options.name: Targeted adjustment
options.description: Fund adjustments for engineers furthest below market, decided case by case by the head of people.

options.name: Everyone to market
options.description: Raise every engineer to the market median in this review.

options.description: Pay one-off retention bonuses and leave salaries unchanged.

recommendation.rationale: Turnover above the company rate, the part pay could plausibly reduce, cost about [F14] last year against a rough [F6] to move everyone, so a targeted adjustment fits the budget better; the head of people decides each person's pay.
